newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-Bunce improves with age.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-Bunce improves with age.

text.p: Johannesburg, July 20 - At 35 he's in good nick. Good enough to match some legs 10 years younger on the test rugby scene.
South African Percy Montgomery, 15 years his junior, and the entire Springboks team hell-bent for victory found that out at Ellis Park yesterday.
Bunce carved through them and scored two magnificent tries in the All Blacks' 35-32 Tri-Series victory.
"We picked him for today a long time ago because we know what he can do and how important he is to the side," Hart said of the centre after the win.
"I think his performance was absolutely special, not only on attack but he made some huge tackles in the second half.
"He made a slow start to the game, turned over the ball twice and missed a tackle later, but apart from that he played brilliantly."
Bunce said he acknowledged some flak he copped when there was a call to replace him with Auckland's Eroni Clarke.
"You take a little notice of them, but the selectors put faith in me and I hope that goes a little way to repay them," a modest Bunce said.
The two times he turned over possession took the sweetness of the victory and his two tries from him after the match.
He said he took the tackle the first time and placed the ball back and didn't realise the Springboks had stolen it.
"The second time I went in too high and I just got held up. That was disappointing because we've worked at training going in low."
He said his game plan also disappeared for a while when he took a gap and isolated himself rather than sticking to the targets to recycle the ball to create more options.
Bunce's first try was a gem. Olo Brown and Taine Randell set up second phase and he cut through from 30 metres from the next phase.
His second, a diagonal run for 60 metres, was paved by his experience.
"I hadn't backed myself to go all the way but it just kept opening and I just kept going. I think Taine Randell made that one because he was inside and (fullback) James Small was distracted."
